title: Strain-tuned mechanical, ferromagnetic, thermoelectric and pressure-induced thermodynamic properties of the double perovskite Ba 2 InMoO 6  for energy-harvesting purposes
content: The biaxial strain in oxide-based double perovskites provides significant insight into their electronic and magnetic properties, showing their potential for spintronic applications. A first-principles study of the mechanical, ferromagnetic, thermoelectric and thermodynamic properties of the double perovskite Ba2InMoO6 has been conducted using the WIEN2K simulation package. The structural properties are illustrated via lattice parameters, ground-state energies and optimized curves. The computed values of the elastic constants (C11, C12 and C44) verify the crystal rigidity, mechanical stability and elastic behaviour, as well as the bonding nature, of the materials. A Pugh's ratio greater than 1.75, a positive Cauchy pressure, and a Poisson's ratio greater than the critical value of 0.26 confirm the ductility of the studied compound. Furthermore, the ferromagnetic phase exhibits an integer total magnetic moment, with the Mo atom contributing predominantly to the net moment. The half-metallic performance of Ba2InMoO6 is revealed by its bandgap calculated using the TB-mBJ approximation, which makes it an appropriate candidate for spintronic applications. The thermoelectric transport coefficients calculated based on the semi-classical Boltzmann transport model show that n-type conductivity is dominant and the Seebeck coefficient is significant, indicating the good transport behavior of the electrons and possible practicality of Ba2InMoO6 in thermoelectric energy harvesting. In the calculations of the thermodynamic properties, both Cp and Cv approach the classical Dulong–Petit limit at higher temperatures.
